corrections: Computed the batch as the exact page-node difference between knowledge/nodes/algo.json and the four earlier algorithm audits; all 24 remaining page nodes are recorded here.

Corrected the suffix-array visualization to describe its actual implementation: direct suffix comparison is worst-case O(n^2 log n), and its pairwise LCP loop is worst-case O(n^2) and is not Kasai's algorithm.
Included occurrence-output cost in suffix-array substring queries instead of presenting O(m log n) as the complete cost.
Qualified rolling-hash collision probabilities: fixed parameters do not provide an unconditional 1/M or 1/(M1*M2) guarantee, and double hashing reduces rather than eliminates collisions.
Qualified bit-operation O(1) complexity to the fixed-word RAM model; arbitrary-precision integer operations depend on operand bit length.

Corrected backtracking's blanket O(n) space claim and made enumeration bounds output-sensitive; pruning improves explored search but does not generally turn exponential worst cases into polynomial ones.
Removed the general claim that greedy algorithms are necessarily asymptotically faster than dynamic programming; correctness and complexity are problem-specific.
Marked capacity-indexed 0/1 knapsack DP O(nW) as pseudo-polynomial because W is a numeric value rather than its encoding length.
Corrected the sliding-window median discussion: balanced trees or dual heaps with lazy deletion support O(log k) updates, so re-sorting every window is not required.
Separated probabilistic guarantees for Bloom filters, HyperLogLog and Count-Min Sketch; added hash-model and nonnegative-update preconditions and removed a fixed HashSet memory estimate.

Reviewed the remaining binary search, KMP, tree traversal, LCS/LIS, monotonic structures, heavy hitters, Fenwick tree, Aho-Corasick, two pointers, divide-and-conquer, edit distance, interval DP, bipartite matching and heavy-light decomposition pages; retained their stated bounds with their demonstrated inputs and algorithm variants.

relationSuggestions.reason: The O(n log n) LIS method uses lower-bound binary search over the tails array.
Aho-Corasick extends prefix/failure-transition ideas from one pattern to a trie of patterns.
A monotonic deque maintains extrema for a moving window in amortized linear total time.
Bloom filters are the membership-query member of the broader approximate-data-structure family.
Count-Min Sketch frequency estimates can feed a bounded candidate structure for approximate heavy hitters.
Fenwick trees use the lowbit operation to navigate ranges represented by binary index structure.
0/1 knapsack generally needs dynamic programming, whereas fractional knapsack admits a greedy solution.
Both use a two-dimensional prefix-state dynamic program but optimize different recurrences.
Heavy-light decomposition computes subtree sizes, parents and heavy children through tree traversals.
Rolling hashes provide probabilistic substring fingerprints, while suffix arrays provide a deterministic sorted-suffix index.
